answer: Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 20 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Because the voyage stamp is verified against the pigment nonce, the ivory audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm therefore pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Honest users pay that once, farms 13 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
